commit_attribution: The primary human-authorized operator session (claude-local) performed Section-0 governance validation (branch/HEAD/origin-main sync, clean-tree confirmation, predecessor-completion cross-check via PROJECT_STATUS.md and git log, independent CPIPC derivation and validation via pcae.core.phase_id: is_valid True on predecessor and candidate, same_series True, same_branch True, compare=less, equals=False, zero collisions against `git log --all`), created and scoped the governed task (docs/tests/tasks zones only, all src/pcae/core/hpac_pawa_helper_*.py and hpac_pawa_schemas.py/hpac_pawa_agent_exclusion.py explicitly forbidden), and delegated the bulk of the architecture analysis and contract drafting (writer-authority inventory, mint-path search, REQ-033 reconstruction, Models A-D comparison and selection, 30-item threat matrix, requirement/invariant freeze, structural tests) to one bounded fork worker under the phase-authorization prompt's own Section 78 delegated-worker constraints (no production code, no commit/push, no finalization, no successor IV). The primary operator then independently re-read the full diff against the delegated worker's own report rather than trusting its summary, and discovered a real defect: the worker recorded a truncated ANCESTOR phase ID (145 characters) as the contract's 'Frozen by' identity instead of the independently-validated candidate CPIPC (185 characters, predecessor + literal '.1'). The primary operator fixed this directly (Edit tool), recomputed the contract file's sha256 (verified against the new value programmatically), and corrected two now-stale sha256 references inside the phase architecture doc that the fix invalidated -- catching this only because the primary operator re-ran the worker's own new test suite after the fix and one test failed until the doc's hash references were corrected too. The primary operator then independently re-ran the full 39-test contract test suite, ran the hpac_pawa_helper-scoped regression suite (96 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed), committed under the corrected phase ID, and ran `pcae phase fast-green-attribution` directly (never delegated) -- twice: once flagging one attributable failure (test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_verify_detects_tampered_record), then a second time using the tool's own --rerun-node isolation mechanism, which reclassified it as an environment/flaky failure (0 attributable failures on the isolated rerun, test passed standalone in an earlier direct check too). All load-bearing claims in this report were independently re-derived or re-executed by the primary operator, not merely accepted from the delegated worker.
summary: Architecture + contract evolution only phase. Resolved (at the contract level, not implementation) the writer-authority blocker preventing HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-001's one-shot helper from performing admin_mutation, certification_write, and presentation_evidence_write. Independently reconstructed the current writer-authority inventory and exact mint-path (legacy hpac_protected_admin_writer.py sealed factory, gated by _PRODUCTION_WRITER_FACTORY_SEAL) and REQ-033's exact text and scope. Evaluated Models A-D; selected Model D -- an evolved HPACWriterCapability minted via a second, additive, narrower low-level primitive gated by a new, distinct seal, owned by a new helper-only module, requiring zero canonical-store production code changes since store-side recognition (require_writer/record_write) already keys on seal identity plus a process-local issuance registry rather than mint entrypoint. REQ-033 disposition: Option B (additive clarifying requirement, HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-REQ-129, byte-unchanged intent) -- REQ-033's own text does not forbid a new, narrowly-scoped, non-agent-reachable mint pathway. HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-001 v1.0 -> v2.0 (MAJOR): +REQ-115-140 and +REQ-114A (141 requirements total, contiguous, verified), +PAWAH-INV-11 through INV-18, a 30-item threat matrix (Section 54 of the phase-authorization prompt), and full requirement-to-future-test traceability. HPAC-PAWA-001 v2.0 and HPAC-PPA-001 v2.0 remain byte-unchanged (both confirmed via sha256). Zero production source changed; zero caller migration; zero live deployment; zero real ceremony/authentication/certification. N-16-5 remains NOT CLOSED. Successor N16-5-F-5-TB-HELPER-WRITER-AUTHORITY-CONTRACT-IV derived but explicitly NOT begun, per the phase-authorization prompt's Section 85 absolute stop boundary.
